facts.raw_span: left testicular bloating and dull pain for 20 years
acutely worsening over the past 10 days
denied other medical history
left testis was enlarged, firm, smooth, without discrete nodules or tenderness
transillumination was negative
right testis, epididymides, and vas deferens were normal
bilateral epididymal cysts (largest 0.67 × 0.46 cm)
a 1.09 × 0.79 cm well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow
a small left hydrocele
serum CA19-9 level of 57.5 U/mL (normal <27 U/mL)
alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers were within normal limits

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a painless testicular mass, along with the ultrasound findings of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow and elevated CA19-9 levels, suggests testicular cancer.
The presence of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow and normal alpha-fetoprotein levels is consistent with seminoma, a type of testicular cancer.

The elevated CA19-9 levels and the presence of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow suggest a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, although the normal alpha-fetoprotein levels make this less likely.

The presence of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow and a small hydrocele could be consistent with an epidermoid cyst of the testis, although the elevated CA19-9 levels are not typically associated with this condition.
The presence of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow and elevated CA19-9 levels could be consistent with a Leydig cell tumor, although this is a less common diagnosis.
